ai.description: *Uropeltis petersi* is a small, cylindrical snake reaching 20–30 cm. It is dark brown to black with yellow lateral spots and possesses a truncated, shield-like tail tip used for burrowing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis petersi* is best distinguished by its uniquely enlarged, shield-like terminal scale that is abruptly truncated and heavily keeled, unlike the rounded tails of others.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis petersi* inhabits the moist evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis petersi* is a fossorial snake that spends most of its life underground, emerging primarily at night or after heavy rains to forage for earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis petersi* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis petersi* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation montane forests.
